title: Expert Brain Object
description:
The smallest reusable knowledge unit. TWENTY-THREE sections.

SCOPE decides where the file lives:
  scope: core        objects/core/<name>.yaml           loaded by MORE THAN ONE capability
  scope: capability  objects/<capability>/<name>.yaml   loaded by EXACTLY ONE
validate.py enforces this from the reference graph, not from intent — a scoped object two capabilities load is an error, a core object one capability loads is a warning. A distinction nobody can violate is the only kind that survives a hundred more objects.

ATTRIBUTES replaces the old Components + Properties pair. One structured field list, not two overlapping ones: an attribute is `composite` when it groups other attributes and `value` when it holds data. The earlier split had Components-as-folders and Properties-as-fields, which meant every real field appeared twice and the two copies disagreed within a week.

SEVEN sections are required so a first pass can be incremental: identity, purpose, attributes, relationships, inference_patterns, evidence, metadata. The other sixteen may be absent. A thin object is still worse than none — it looks finished — so author all twenty-three when you can.

Vocabulary membership (ops, obs kinds, fact paths, verbs) is enforced by _tools/validate.py against _schema/vocabulary.yaml, not here.

id.description: <domain>.obj.<scope>.<snake_name>, where <scope> is the literal 'core' or the capability leaf name. The scope segment makes the id self-locating and lets the same noun exist in two capabilities without collision — sales.obj.negotiation.concession and sales.obj.objection_handling.objection are different knowledge.

owner_capability.description: Required when scope = capability: the one capability that loads it. On a core object this is advisory and names who owns review.

subdomain.description: Advisory. A core object may be loaded by capabilities in any subdomain.

aliases.description: What the profession also calls this. Feeds terminology resolution and stops two teams authoring the same object twice under different names.

supersedes.description: Object id this replaces, when a rename or split happened.

purpose.description: What this object IS and what it is FOR. Replaces the old free-text description with something a reviewer can argue with.

discriminator.description: The single sentence that separates this object from the one it is most often confused with. Usually the most valuable line in the file — 'a VP who cannot sign is a Stakeholder, not a Decision Maker'.

answers.description: The questions loading this object lets Layer 4 answer. If you cannot name one, the object is documentation.

not.description: What this object explicitly is NOT responsible for, and which object owns that instead.

attributes.description: The object's structure AND its data, in one list. `composite` attributes group others via `contains`; `value` attributes hold data. Formerly two sections (Components + Properties) that duplicated every field.

states.description: The lifecycle this object moves through. Absent when the object genuinely has none — a Mental Model has no states and inventing them is noise.

implies.description: What being in this state means for the deal or account, in business terms.

relationships.description: Typed edges to other objects. Eleven fields, because a relationship that carries no weight, confidence or condition is decoration — Layer 4 cannot reason over it, it can only display it.

inference_patterns.description: How this object is DISCOVERED when nobody states it. Every pattern carries a human `statement` and, when executable, a machine `when` in the engine's whitelisted grammar. Prose alone cannot fire — there is no runtime that evaluates an English sentence except a model, and reaching for one here defeats the architecture.

inputs.description: Where this object gets filled from.

outputs.description: What this object can tell the rest of the stack.

preconditions.description: What must already be true before this object can be meaningfully resolved. Distinct from constraints: a precondition gates whether we can even ask, a constraint bounds the answer.

requires.description: Object ids or attribute names that must be resolved first.

if_unmet.description: What to do when it is not satisfied. `block` and `degrade` are different answers and the difference is the whole of Layer 3 strategy S8.

constraints.description: Limits on what is possible or permitted. A hard constraint eliminates a Layer 4 candidate; a soft one only lowers its score.

business_rules.description: Deterministic rules local to this object. No model evaluates these. A rule spanning two objects belongs in rules/, not here — authored in one place it can see both sides of its own condition.

rule_ref.description: Id of a cross-object rule in rules/ that this one participates in.

decision_factors.description: What Layer 4 should weigh when this object is in play. Advisory inputs to a reasoning unit, never a decision — Rule 05.

evidence.description: What counts as a receipt for this object, and what each source is worth. Rule 04 — confidence without receipts is a guess.

independent_of.description: Sources this one is genuinely independent of. Rule 11: only independent corroboration may RAISE confidence, so the graph of what-corroborates-what has to be authored rather than assumed.

calibrates.description: Pattern or rule ids this metric is the feedback signal for.

invalidates.description: Attribute names or object ids whose prior value this event makes untrustworthy — a champion departing voids everything they told us about internal politics.

actions.description: What Layer 5 may operationalise. Naming an action here does not authorise it; Layer 5 still plans and Layer 5.2 still gates.

dependencies.description: Other objects and artifacts this one cannot be reasoned about without. Distinct from relationships: a relationship is a fact about the world, a dependency is a fact about the compile.

target.description: Object, playbook, rule or framework id.

exceptions.description: Where the rules above are legitimately wrong. Every experienced operator carries these and no playbook writes them down, which is precisely why the naive system feels stupid to an expert.

overrides.description: Rule, constraint or pattern ids this exception suspends.

best_practices.description: What a good operator does with this object. Atlas lists Best Practices as first-class Expert Brain content.

anti_patterns.description: What a plausible-looking operator does wrong. Usually more diagnostic than the best practice, because it names the specific mistake rather than the general virtue.

why_it_happens.description: The reasonable-sounding logic that leads someone there. An anti-pattern nobody would plausibly commit is not worth recording.

detectable_by.description: Pattern or metric ids that would catch it.

examples.description: Concrete instances, INCLUDING the classic misclassification. An example set with no negative case teaches only the easy half.

references.description: Where this knowledge comes from — the methodology, book, framework or internal source. Makes the object arguable rather than asserted, and tells a reviewer whose opinion they are reading.

artifact_ref.description: Id of a mental model, playbook or framework in this brain that formalises the reference.

attribute.description: One field or one structural grouping. The union of the old Component (9 fields) and Property (7 fields) specs, because two overlapping field lists always disagree within a week.

purpose.description: What it captures and why it matters. Not a restatement of the name.

type.description: composite = groups other attributes via `contains`. value = holds data. derived = computed from other attributes or from Layer 2. reference = points at another object.

contains.description: Attribute names grouped under this one. Only when type = composite.

ref.description: Target object id. Only when type = reference or data_type = ref.

validation.description: A human-readable rule the compiler can later formalise, e.g. '>= 0' or 'must be one of allowed_values'.

constraints.description: Business limits on the value, as opposed to type validation.

source_paths.description: Layer 2 fact paths that populate this attribute. Paths outside the substrate are reported by backlog.py, not rejected — they are the ask.

derived_from.description: Attribute names or fact paths this is computed from. Only when type = derived.

sensitivity.description: Feeds Rule 10 — an attribute never widens the audience of the evidence it came from.

relationship.description: Eleven fields. `source` defaults to the object declaring it. Weight and confidence are basis points because Layer 4 does arithmetic on them.

source.description: Object id. Omit — it defaults to this object. Set it only when authoring an edge on behalf of another object, which should be rare and deliberate.

target.description: Object id. Link integrity is checked by validate.py.

type.description: The verb. Validated against vocabulary.yaml open.relationship_verbs.

weight_bp.description: How much this edge matters relative to the object's other edges. A Champion's route to the Decision Maker outweighs their membership of the committee, and Layer 4 cannot know that unless it is written down.

confidence_bp.description: How sure we are the edge exists at all, as distinct from how much it matters.

conditions.description: When this edge holds. An edge that only exists under a condition and says so is worth more than one asserted unconditionally.

evidence.description: Evidence sources that establish the edge.

priority.description: Traversal order when several edges compete. 1 is first.

predicate.description: One condition in the engine's whitelisted grammar. engine.py:_eval_condition dispatches in this order and returns False for anything it does not recognise — it does not raise. Conditions in a list are ANDed; express OR as two entries.

op.description: IN is uppercase. engine.py:71 tests op == "IN"; a lowercase in falls through to the numeric branch and evaluates False forever.

value.description: A literal, or a learned per-entity baseline resolved as max(floor, mult x baseline).

statement.description: The pattern in plain language, for a human reviewer.

status.description: executable = every path and obs kind in `when` exists in the vocabulary substrate. needs_signal = it cannot fire yet; backlog.py reports it as a Layer 1/2 requirement.

attribute.description: Attribute this pattern sets, or null when it asserts the object itself.

corroborates.description: Other pattern ids this independently supports. Rule 11: confidence may only rise on independent evidence, so independence has to be declared, not inferred.

requires_signals.description: Only when status = needs_signal. What Layer 1 or 2 must start emitting.

false_positive.description: The case where this pattern fires and is wrong. Knowing it is what lets a reviewer set the confidence honestly.
